findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
findings.comment: Observed the bar triple sink to have a too low concentration of quaternary ammonium (100ppm). Water was hot to the touch. Triple sink had 4 tablets in it. CORRECTED: PIC and Staff were educated that the water temperature for quaternary ammonium-based sanitizing solutions needs to be room temperature to be effective (65-75 F). Staff remade the triple sink using cool water and 3 tablets (sink was mostly full) and it tested at 200ppm. Ensure that chemical sanitizing solutions are used per manufacturer’s instructions; for quaternary ammonium that is 65-75 F for water temperature and a concentration between 200-400ppm.
findings.citation_text: 4-501.114(C) Manual and Mechanical Warewashing Equipment, Chemical Sanitization - Temperature, pH, Concentration, and Hardness. A chemical SANITIZER used in a SANITIZING solution for a manual or mechanical operation at contact times specified under 4-703.11(C) shall meet the criteria specified under §7-204.11 Sanitizers, Criteria, shall be used in accordance with the EPA-registered label use instructions, and shall be used as follows: (C) A quaternary ammonium compound solution shall: (1) Have a minimum temperature of 24°C (75°F), (2) Have a concentration as specified under § 7-204.11 and as indicated by the manufacturer's use directions included in the labeling, and (3) Be used only in water with 500 MG/L hardness or less or in water having a hardness no greater than specified by the EPA-registered label use instructions. [P]

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean.
findings.comment:
Observed the following non-food contact surfaces must be cleaned:
(i) 1ST REPEAT: The upper nonfood-contact surfaces above the soda nozzles have mineral buildup.
(ii) The coil on the ceiling of the walk-in cooler is dusty.
(iii) The box fan used in the dish room is dusty.
(iv) The walls near the fryers that are not stainless steel have an accumulation of grease and soil residues.
(v) The deep freezers have an accumulation of ice around the edges that can fall onto the food.
Non-food contact surfaces must be cleaned at a frequency necessary to avoid the accumulation of dust, dirt, food residue, and other debris. Ensure that the above referenced are cleaned to sight and touch by the next routine inspection.
findings.citation_text: 4-601.11(C) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (C) NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be kept free of an accumulation of dust, dirt, FOOD residue, and other debris. [C]

findings.title: Proper date marking and disposition.
findings.comment:
Inspectors observed multiple temperature controls for food safety (TCS) to lack date marking, including but not limited to:
1) sausage at the long prep cooler
2) buttermilk in the standing 2 door cooler
3) carrot cake in the walk in cooler
CORRECTED- dates were placed on all of the aforementioned items. Ensure all TCS items are date marked with the day of preparation to be used or discarded within seven days.
findings.citation_text: 3-501.18(A) Ready-to-Eat, Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Disposition. (A) A FOOD specified in 3-501.17(A) or (B) shall be discarded if it: (1) Exceeds the temperature and time combination specified in 3-501.17(A), except time that the product is frozen; (2) Is in a container or PACKAGE that does not bear a date or day; or (3) Is inappropriately marked with a date or day that exceeds a temperature and time combination as specified in 3-501.17(A).[P]

findings.title: Toxic substances properly identified, stored and used.
findings.comment: Inspectors observed that two of the sanitizer buckets (quaternary ammonia) were at concentrations exceeding the maximum toxicity level for a food-contact surface, as specified by manufacturer. CORRECTED: PIC was notified and the concentration of both sanitizer buckets was adjusted. Inspector and PIC clarified how many sanitizing tablets should be used in each sanitizer bucket (2 tablets). Ensure that all sanitizers shall meet the requirements for use on food-contact surfaces.
findings.citation_text: 7-204.11 Sanitizers, Criteria. Chemical SANITIZERS, including chemical sanitizing solutions generated on-site, and other chemical antimicrobials applied to FOOD-CONTACT SURFACEs shall: (A) Meet the requirements specified in 40 CFR 180.940 Tolerance exemptions for active and inert ingredients for use in antimicrobial formulations (Food-contact surface sanitizing solutions).

findings.title: Allergen awareness training for CFPM
findings.comment:
PIC was unable to produce record of an Allergen Awareness Training. PIC will provide a record of Allergen Awareness Training by the next routing inspection. Ensure that all CFPMs have training in Allergen Awareness within 30 days of employment, and renew it every 3 years.

410 ILCS 625/3.07(b). Allergen awareness training. (b) Unless otherwise provided, all certified food service sanitation managers employed by a restaurant must receive or obtain training in basic allergen awareness principles within 30 days after employment and every 3 years thereafter. Training programs must be accredited by the American National Standards Institute or another reputable accreditation agency under the ASTM International E2659-09 (Standard Practice for Certificate Programs). There is no limit to how many times an employee may take the training.

findings.title: Hands clean and properly washed.
findings.comment: Observed an employee handling raw bacon and then proceeded to grab sandwich bread from the toaster wearing the same gloves. The employee was educated about the importance of removing gloves, washing hands, and donning new gloves when switching between handling raw meats to ready-to-eat foods. The bread was discarded during the inspection. Ensure that hands are always clean to avoid contamination.
findings.citation_text: 2-301.14 When to Wash. FOOD EMPLOYEES shall clean their hands and exposed portions of their arms as specified under § 2-301.12 immediately before engaging in FOOD preparation including working with exposed FOOD, clean EQUIPMENT and UTENSILS, and unwrapped SINGLE-SERVICE and SINGLE-USE ARTICLES and: (A) After touching bare human body parts other than clean hands and clean, exposed portions of arms; (B) After using the toilet room; (C) After caring for or handling SERVICE ANIMALS or aquatic animals as specified in 2-403.11(B); (D) Except as specified in 2-401.11(B), after coughing, sneezing, using a handkerchief or disposable tissue, using TOBACCO PRODUCTS, eating, or drinking; (E) After handling soiled EQUIPMENT or UTENSILS; (F) During FOOD preparation, as often as necessary to remove soil and contamination and to prevent cross contamination when changing tasks; (G) When switching between working with raw FOOD and working with READY-TO-EAT FOOD; (H) Before donning gloves to initiate a task that involves working with FOOD; and (I) After engaging in other activities that contaminate the hands.

findings.title: No bare-hand contact with RTE food or a pre-approved alternative procedure properly allowed.
findings.comment: Observed an employee grab sandwich bread with their bare hands. The employee was educated that ready-to-eat foods must always be handed with a barrier (i.e., single-use gloves, utensils, or deli tissue). The bread was discarded during the inspection and the employee donned gloves to grab a new piece of bread. Ensure that employees always use a barrier when handling ready-it-eat foods.
findings.citation_text: 3-301.11(B) Preventing Contamination from Hands. (B) Except when washing fruits and vegetables as specified under §3-302.15 or as specified in (D) and (E) of this section, FOOD EMPLOYEES may not contact exposed, READY-TO-EAT FOOD with their bare hands and shall use suitable UTENSILS such as deli tissue, spatulas, tongs, single-use gloves, or dispensing EQUIPMENT.

findings.title: No bare-hand contact with RTE food or a pre-approved alternative procedure properly allowed.
findings.comment: Observed the scoop for the sugar container does not have a handle. The inspector educated that all scoops for ready-to-eat foods must have a handle that is stored above the top of the food to avoid bare hands contacting the food. Ensure that the sugar container has a proper scoop by the next routine inspection.
findings.citation_text: 3-301.11(C) Preventing Contamination from Hands. (C) FOOD EMPLOYEES shall minimize bare hand and arm contact with exposed FOOD that is not in a READY-TO-EAT form.

findings.title: Food properly labeled; original container.
findings.comment: THIS IS A FIRST REPEAT VIOLATION: Observed sugar by the large prep cooler and flour by the fryers were stored unpackaged in containers without labeling. All easily mistakable foods (ex. white powders) not in the original container must be labeled with the common name of the food. The salt and flour containers were properly labeled during the inspection. Ensure that easily mistaken foods removed from original packaging are always labeled with the common name.
findings.citation_text: 3-302.12 Food Storage Containers, Identified with Common Name of Food. Except for containers holding FOOD that can be readily and unmistakably recognized such as dry pasta, working containers holding FOOD or FOOD ingredients that are removed from their original packages for use in the FOOD ESTABLISHMENT, such as cooking oils, flour, herbs, potato flakes, salt, spices, and sugar shall be identified with the common name of the FOOD.

findings.title: Proper date marking and disposition.
findings.comment: Observed a jug of milk that was opened on Monday in the double cooler lacked date marking. The milk was properly date marked during the inspection. Ensure that temperature control for safety, ready-to-eat foods kept at the facility for longer than 24 hours are always date marked to indicate the seven day maximum (with the day the food was opened/prepared being day one).
findings.citation_text: 3-501.17(A) Ready-to-Eat, Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Date Marking. (A) Except when PACKAGING FOOD using a REDUCED OXYGEN PACKAGING method as specified under § 3-502.12, and except as specified in (E) and (F) of this section, refrigerated, READY-TO-EAT, TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD prepared and held in a FOOD ESTABLISHMENT for more than 24 hours shall be clearly marked to indicate the date or day by which the FOOD shall be consumed on the PREMISES, sold, or discarded when held at a temperature of 5C (41F) or less for a maximum of 7 days. The day of preparation shall be counted as Day 1.
